problem: RL-based social navigation is short-sighted: agents react only to current human positions and often collide or block humans' paths. Existing SocialNav datasets also lack realism (few scenes, unnatural human motion, imbalanced density) and often assume global information.
motivation: In crowded indoor spaces robots must anticipate where humans will go, not just where they are. Trajectory forecasting helps outdoors (driving) but had not been integrated into indoor egocentric RL SocialNav, and a realistic benchmark with natural human motion was missing.
key_idea: Train an RL PointNav agent with future-aware supervision: auxiliary tasks that predict human count, current positions and future trajectories, plus a reward penalty for obstructing humans' predicted future paths.
insight: Explicit future trajectory forecasting is the most helpful single auxiliary task (Suc. 40.94 -> 54.00 over the PointNav baseline), which shows that learning future human dynamics matters more than only sensing current proximity. The auxiliary tasks combined give little gain over the best single ones (53.63 vs 54.00), and only adding the Social Cognition Penalty pushes the model to 55.15 and speeds convergence. So the reward shaping is needed to make the auxiliary tasks effective.
method: Main policy network: ResNet-50 encodes depth, a linear layer encodes the point goal, a 2-layer LSTM feeds actor and value heads; trained with DD-PPO, initialized from a PointNav model and fine-tuned 10M steps.

Social Cognition Penalty (SCP): PointNav reward minus penalties for collisions with obstacles/humans, human proximity (exp(-d) within 2 m), and trajectory obstruction (overlap with humans' future H-step paths within 0.05 m, weighted by 1/(k-t+1)); penalties are off within 2 m of the goal.
Human Count Estimation (auxiliary): an LSTM plus self-attention on the policy's LSTM hidden state classifies the number of humans (0..6) with cross-entropy.
Current Position Tracking (auxiliary): takes the hidden state and the oracle human count and regresses each human's 2D position relative to the robot with masked MSE.
Future Trajectory Forecasting (auxiliary): a bi-directional stacked LSTM plus attention takes the hidden state, count and current positions and regresses H-step future trajectories with masked MSE.
Total loss: beta_main*L_PPO + beta_aux*(L_count+L_pos+L_traj); the auxiliary heads are used only in training.

Social-HM3D / Social-MP3D benchmark: Habitat 3.0 scenes (844 HM3D, 72 MP3D) with up to 6 humans scaled by scene area, two goals per human, ORCA avoidance, walking animations, speeds 0.8-1.2x robot speed.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + LSTM actor-critic with auxiliary LSTM/attention heads (trained with DD-PPO, initialized from a PointNav model)
setting.training_data: Social-HM3D train split, 10M RL steps of fine-tuning on top of pre-trained PointNav weights; Social-MP3D used zero-shot
setting.privileged: none at test time; oracle human count, positions and future trajectories are used only for auxiliary training targets and the SCP reward

numbers.backbone: ResNet-50 + LSTM, DD-PPO with SPM + SCP
numbers.extra: Trained on Social-HM3D train; mean over 3 seeds
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Performance Evaluation of SocialNav Tasks), Social-HM3D, Falcon row

numbers.backbone: ResNet-50 + LSTM, DD-PPO with SPM + SCP
numbers.extra: Trained only on Social-HM3D; zero-shot transfer to Social-MP3D

numbers_note: Benchmark is the paper's own new SocialNav benchmark, so it is labeled 'other:'. The split is a test set; the paper says 'Social-HM3D test set'.
results: Falcon reaches 55.15% success on Social-HM3D and 55.05% zero-shot on Social-MP3D, well above the RL baseline Proximity-Aware (20.11 / 18.45) and above A* (46.14 / 43.85) and ORCA (38.91 / 40.38). PSC stays about 90%, but H-Coll (42.96) is higher than Proximity-Aware's 33.99.
limitations: Proximity-Aware has lower human collision rate and higher PSC despite much lower success, showing the metrics trade off task success against social comfort.
The benchmark has no higher-level human behaviors such as yielding.
Training uses oracle human positions and trajectories from the simulator for the auxiliary tasks and penalties.
